revision_note: Rationale text, gap units and metadata wording corrected after review: all figures in the rationales are computed from the delivered items instead of typed by hand, calendar-day gaps replace floored elapsed-day gaps, and unsupported wording about sensor resolution, LUT semantics and land cover was removed.
auth: public metadata only, no bearer token requested, no product downloaded, no pixel data inspected
gap_unit_note: Gaps are calendar-day differences between acquisition dates. Elapsed intervals between the acquisition timestamps are a few seconds short of the calendar figure (the timestamps differ by 4-24 s within a series), so a naive elapsed-days floor would understate them by one day.

overlap_method.operation: full polygon intersection, not bbox intersection
overlap_method.area_projection: Lambert azimuthal equal-area on WGS84 sphere (R=6370997 m) centred on the mean centroid of the series, so hectares are equal-area and the projection origin stays within about 1 degree of the data
overlap_method.footprint_source: STAC item geometry (Polygon, EPSG:4326 / storageCrs CRS84) as returned by the public API; these are frame outlines, so overlap areas are outline-derived and are an upper bound on the true common footprint
overlap_method.invalid_geometry_policy: shapely.make_valid applied if a geometry failed is_valid

primary_series.selection_rationale: Preferred series: the smallest SGF product family in this collection. The group holds 9 acquisitions from 2009-08-12 to 2010-02-20 (192 calendar days) on an exact 24-calendar-day cadence, all sharing product_type SGF, product_format GeoTIFF, beam W3 / Wide3, polarization VV VH, ascending orbit direction and relative orbit 98, with grid spacing 12.5 m pixel x 12.5 m line and applied_lut Constant-beta on every date. The selected dates are 2009-08-12, 2009-11-16 and 2010-02-20; first, middle and last dates were taken to maximise the temporal baseline: 96 calendar days between epochs, 192 calendar days in total. Minimum pairwise polygon overlap of the selected trio is 1 442 704 ha, which is 99.64% of the smaller footprint; the minimum is set by the 2009-08-12 scene, whose footprint bounds the 3-way AOI, while the two later scenes overlap each other at 99.92%. Exactly one frame exists per date in this group, so no adjacent-frame choice is needed. Scene sizes are 355, 395 and 395 MB, versus 5497 MB each for the three comparison SLC scenes, so this trio is about 14x smaller to download. The union of the three selected scene footprints has bounds 118.12 / 4.814 / 119.506 / 6.147 (lon/lat, WGS84), while the 3-way intersection is smaller - its bounds are in aoi_intersection_bbox_lonlat. The region is in the Malaysian state of Sabah on the island of Borneo as read from those coordinates. No land-cover or forest-extent claim is made: the catalog exposes only frame outlines and a browse thumbnail, so the habitat of this AOI is unverified here.

comparison_series.selection_rationale: Comparison series, modern SLC, same rules applied to the Extra-Fine population. The group holds 32 acquisitions from 2013-09-08 to 2016-04-25 (960 calendar days) on a nominal 24-day repeat, with actual date gaps of 24, 48, 72 and 96 calendar days. All share product_type SLC, product_format GeoTIFF, beam XF0W2 / Extra Fine0, polarization HH, ascending direction and relative orbit 104, grid spacing 2.662357 m pixel x 2.498430-2.498449 m line and applied_lut Land. Frames within one pass (1 to 8 per date) are adjacent along-track swaths, so frames were clustered into ground swaths by polygon centroid and a single swath present on all three dates was required. The selected dates are 2014-05-06, 2015-04-07 and 2016-04-01. The naive first/middle/last date pick (2013-09-08, 2015-01-25, 2016-04-25) was rejected: its minimum pairwise overlap is 0 ha because the middle date's nearest-centroid frame belongs to a different swath - direct evidence that centroid or bbox matching is unsafe. The selected trio is 336 and 360 calendar days between epochs, 696 calendar days in total, with minimum pairwise polygon overlap 1 666 598 ha = 99.86% of the smaller footprint, and all three scenes are 5497 MB each. The union of the three selected scene footprints has bounds -57.726 / -2.607 / -56.378 / -1.175 (lon/lat, WGS84), while the 3-way intersection bounds are in aoi_intersection_bbox_lonlat. The region is in the Brazilian Amazon basin as read from those coordinates; land cover is not verified by this catalog. The two series are alternatives, not a mergeable stack: different product class, beam, polarization, region, epoch and grid.
comparison_series.frame_selection_rule: frames of a pass clustered into ground swaths by polygon centroid (0.02 deg tolerance); a swath had to exist on all three dates, epochs had to be >=300 calendar days apart and every pairwise polygon overlap had to be non-empty; the surviving triple with the largest minimum pairwise overlap won

rejected_naive_date_pick.reason: the middle date's nearest-centroid frame lies on a different ground swath, so overlap collapses to ~0 ha; a real polygon intersection on one consistent swath is required

metadata_unknowns: No calibrated radiometry, incidence angle, look direction, SNR, orbit phase or calibration-LUT identifier in the STAC properties. Radiometric terrain correction and layover/shadow masking cannot be planned from metadata alone.

applied_lut is recorded as a label only ('Land' on the modern SLC items, 'Constant-beta' on the legacy items). The catalog does not define the vocabulary or state which coefficients, speckle filtering or multilooking were actually applied inside the delivered zip; the meaning of the coefficients is unknown pending product metadata.

sampled_pixel_spacing and sampled_line_spacing are the grid spacing of the delivered GeoTIFF. They are not a resolution figure: native sensor resolution, processing-window limits and looks per pixel are not published, so no resolution can be derived from these fields.
No preview or backscatter asset beyond a browse thumbnail PNG; no per-date radiometric summary, so radiometric comparability between dates is unverified.

product_format is GeoTIFF for both SGF and SLC here, but the zip layout, band naming (amplitude vs real/imag), nodata conventions and calibration file names are undocumented and only visible after an authenticated download.
Product availability on the server and the download path require a bearer token; ordering feasibility (cost, delivery time) is unverified because authentication was out of scope.

Land cover, forest extent and habitat at either AOI are not verifiable from this catalog: only frame outlines and a browse thumbnail are exposed, and no land-cover dataset was consulted within the query budget.

Whether the 800-item central-Amazon bbox sample is the complete archive for that AOI is unknown: paging stopped at 800 items (2016-06-02) and the collection temporal extent is open-ended from 2008-02-14.
An SGF series over the Amazon basin is neither confirmed nor excluded: all SGF groups found in the 200-item legacy sample were in Borneo, and the query budget did not allow a wider search.
no_change_event_asserted: This is a scene-selection deliverable only. Polygon overlap shows the same ground is imaged on the listed dates; it does not show that forest loss, gain or any other real-world change occurred between them. Detecting change requires ordering, radiometric calibration and pixel inspection, none of which was done here.
